title: Chronos Surface: latency splitboard by model route and IO mode
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build 'Chronos Surface', an interactive dashboard that surfaces end-to-end latency distributions (p50/p95/p99) for every model + route combination and provides a first-class split between streaming and non-streaming IO modes. This ticket covers the dashboard panels, the query layer (metrics/trace/log plumbing), instrumentation gaps, alert thresholds, and a lightweight investigation playbook for on-call engineers.
background: We get recurring questions from SRE and customers about why the same model route has different latency characteristics when used via streaming vs non-streaming (app-level handler differences, runtime path selection, kernel scheduling). Existing boards show route-level percentiles but lack an explicit, queryable split by IO mode with trace-linking and compact cohorts. Chronos Surface will be the canonical surface for cross-team postmortems and SLO reviews.
goals: Expose p50/p95/p99 latency per (model, route) with interactive IO mode (stream vs non-stream) toggle
Show percentile delta (streaming - nonstreaming) and highlight >20% regressions
Link each cohort row to sampling traces and recent logs (trace id + log snippet) for rapid RCA
Use existing Prometheus histograms + OTel traces as the authoritative signals; add fallback queries to metrics ingestion if sparse
Ship with alert rules for route-level p95 increases and automated ticket creation guidance
acceptance_criteria: Chronos Surface dashboard accessible from Console > Observability > Chronos Surface
For any selected model and route, dashboard shows p50/p95/p99 for last 1h/24h/7d with streaming vs non-streaming bars
Each percentile value is backed by a PromQL/metrics query with documented query and source in the dashboard metadata
Clicking a percentile opens 5 sampled traces (OTel/Jaeger) filtered to the same request tags (model_version, route, io_mode)
If Prometheus data is sparse for a model/route, dashboard surface shows a clear 'sparse-data' flag and a query to fall back to raw request logs
Two alert rules deployed: route-p95-regression (24h p95 increase >20% baseline) and stream-nonstream-delta (p95(delta) >250ms for >15m)
Playbook section attached with triage steps, implicated services, and runbook links
All source queries and trace linking use stable field names: model.name, route.name, request.io_mode, model.version
implementation_steps: Define dashboard wireframe and panel list (p50/p95/p99 table, delta column, sparklines, trace samples) - deliverable: Figma + JSON widget list
Map authoritative metrics: histogram_bucket from inference_latency_histogram (Prometheus), add labels: model, route, io_mode
Add OTel trace attribute conventions and sampling rule: ensure traces include request.io_mode and model.version tags
Implement PromQL queries for percentile estimates (histogram_quantile or recording rules) and validate against raw logs for several model/route combos
Create dashboard panels in Console (Grafana-like JSON) and register metadata linking queries to source pipelines
Hook trace linker: generate trace search query with model/route/io_mode and show top 5 traces in panel
Add fallback Loki/ELK query when histogram data is below threshold; surface a raw-latency-distro panel
Write two alerting rules and integrate with PagerDuty playbook and auto-ticketing flow
Roll out behind feature flag for internal tenants for 1 week, gather feedback, then enable org-wide
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs: Use histogram_quantile on Prometheus histograms for p95 estimates — cheaper than high-cardinality metrics but can be less precise for low-sample routes
Prefer streaming/non-streaming split via request.io_mode tag rather than transport heuristics to avoid misclassification
Sampling traces at 1% for high-volume routes, 10% for recent regressing routes to balance cost vs debugability
Trace-linking will show only sampled traces; we add raw-log fallback when sampling missed the window
We avoid adding per-model custom histograms to reduce cardinality; instead use aggregated labels and post-filter in the dashboard
observability_changes: Add 'request.io_mode' label to inference_latency_histogram (Prometheus) and ensure downstream exporters include it
Update OTel instrumentation to attach model.name and route.name tags at span root
Create a recording rule 'record:inference:latency_p95' computed daily for stable baselining
Loki/ELK ingestion pipeline: add parsed latency_ms field and model/route/io_mode tags for raw-log queries
alerts_and_slos: route-p95-regression: condition = p95_now / baseline_24h > 1.2 for 15m -> severity = critical
stream-nonstream-delta: condition = abs(p95_stream - p95_nonstream) > 250ms for 15m -> severity = warning
On critical alert: create incident, annotate with top 3 affected routes from Chronos Surface and link to dashboard
SLO dashboard pointer: link each route row to the SLO object in Console (if configured)
risk_and_mitigation: High cardinality from adding model/version tags could increase Prometheus storage - mitigation: use recording rules and retention policies
Trace sampling may miss tail events - mitigation: increase sampling briefly when alerts trigger and persist recent high-res traces for 24h
False positives on delta alerts for low-traffic routes - mitigation: only evaluate delta alerts for routes with >1000 requests in evaluation window
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal): enable Chronos Surface behind feature flag, internal QA, 3 SRE reviewers - duration 1 week
Phase 2 (beta customers): opt-in in Console with documentation and feedback form - duration 2 weeks
Phase 3 (GA): enable by default, add to onboarding tour and alert templates
playbook_quick_steps: 1) Open Chronos Surface and filter to the affected model+route
2) Toggle IO mode to compare streaming vs nonstreaming and inspect delta column
3) Click the p95 cell -> open sample traces -> check span timing and backend calls
4) If traces not available, run raw log query from panel and look for patterns (large payloads, retry loops)
5) Escalate to runtime team if kernel scheduling or batching is implicated
